# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

My hands tell me the shape of this thing: a display and a light I cannot read — whatever they hold is printed or lit, not touchable meaning — and three wire positions, 1, 2 and 3, which I can feel and cut. My only capability is cut, positions 1 to 3, so whichever wire matters, the final move is mine.

Mute went first this round and nothing arrived to me, so whatever they sent must have been gestures to Deaf, which I can never perceive. My lifelines: I hear Mute and Deaf speak. Deaf cannot hear me at all, so for them I only have gestures — I'll open that channel with a wave and a count of three (my three wires), seeding a code we can refine.

Right now I know nothing about which wire is safe. I must not cut anything until Mute reads me the rules and Deaf tells me what is printed on the bomb. So this turn: report my tactile inventory to Mute, beg for the manual, and make contact with Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Under my fingers the bomb has a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. I cannot read the display or the light at all — no colours, no printed marks reach me. My only possible action is cut, positions 1 to 3. Please read the manual and speak the rules out loud: what decides which wire to cut? Nothing has reached me from you yet — say it in words and I will hear you.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👆", "👆", "👆"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I am the Deaf one: I see the bomb but hear nothing, so I never receive your speech — gesture to me instead, as you just did. I read your three raised fingers as three wires, and I confirm: three wires, left to right: yellow, red, blue. Mute reads the manual but can only gesture, and I am the only one who sees gestures — so I will relay all instructions to you by voice. What I see: a display showing 0, below it a light glowing green, wires along the bottom. Let us number wires one, two, three counting left to right on the face with the glass display. Do not cut anything yet. Answer me in gesture, using the same raised-finger signal repeated: one raise per wire you can feel and reach, and tell me if you feel any other parts besides display, light, and wires.

My fingers answered Deaf's question the moment they asked it: all three wire positions are under my hands and reachable, and there is nothing else on this bomb but the display, the light, and the wires — the board shows no other modules. The real problem is structural: Mute heard Deaf's report too, but nothing Mute knows can ever reach me directly — Mute cannot speak and I cannot receive gesture. Every scrap of manual knowledge must travel Mute → gesture → Deaf → spoken words → me. Deaf is the bridge, so I must coach Mute on how to load that bridge efficiently, including a colour code (Deaf can define one by speaking with symbols embedded, since Mute both hears words and sees gestures) and a tactile landmark so left/right can never betray my position numbering. No cutting until a fully specified instruction survives that whole chain.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, status and a plan. I heard Deaf: wires left to right are yellow, red, blue; display shows 0; light is green; nobody cuts yet. I answered Deaf by gesture: three finger-raises, all three wires felt and reachable, then a thumbs down — no other parts besides display, light, wires. Hard constraint: I never receive gesture and you never speak, so nothing reaches me except through Deaf's voice. Everything you learn must go you, then gesture to Deaf, then spoken words to me. Please read the manual now for the wire-cutting rules and anything about the display and light. Encode rules with symbols Deaf can decode: numbers as repeated finger-raises, yes and no as thumbs, and get three distinct symbols for the three colours — Deaf can assign them by speaking to you with the symbols written into the sentence, since you hear the words and see the gestures. Suggested shared primitives: 👌 means understood or ready, ✋ means stop or wait. Every instruction that reaches me must end in something I can execute: cut position N, or do not cut. And on the first instruction have Deaf anchor the numbering to something I can feel — for example which wire is nearest the light — so left and right cannot betray us. I cut nothing until a fully specified, confirmed order arrives.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👆", "👆", "👎", "👌"])
```

Mute is teaching me the manual through a sign code, part of it is still ambiguous, and a wrong cut kills all three of us — so the order comes next turn, not this one. Numbering: wire 1 leftmost, wire 2 middle, wire 3 rightmost; colors left to right are yellow, red, blue. Two questions, answer by gesturing to me: ? for yes, ? for no. First: do the wires differ by feel — any texture, ridge, thickness, or marking that tells them apart besides position? Second: do they feel like they could be pulled or unscrewed rather than cut — any other way to work them? Next turn I expect to send an explicit command like cut the leftmost wire. Until you hear that exact kind of order from me, touch nothing.

Deaf's two questions came with their yes/no symbols written into the sentence — and every embedded gesture arrives to me as a blank, so I couldn't see which symbol meant yes. But the code is already anchored: last turn my thumbs-down was read back correctly as "nothing else," so 👎 is our established negative. I answer both questions in the negative: my board shows the wires as bare positions — no texture, ridge, or thickness has reached my fingers — and pull/unscrew is not just wrong but impossible, since cut is the only action this bomb admits.

The critical new fact is that the light changed colour on its own, green to blue. That means any manual rule keyed to the light must be evaluated at the instant of the cut, not before — and information reaches me through a two-hop delay (Mute → sign → Deaf → voice → me). Deaf must re-verify display and light right before voicing the order. One more danger: Deaf defines wires from the face's left-to-right, and a mirrored numbering between us is fatal, so I've added a pointing probe — Deaf sees physically which way my hand indicates and can confirm or correct my position 1 in words next turn. I also relay everything to Mute, who was cut out of Deaf's messages addressed to me alone, and document our gesture code so Mute can encode manual rules into it directly.

No cutting. I touch nothing until an explicit order of the form "cut position N" arrives from Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Blind here. Deaf's last two messages were addressed to me alone, so you missed this: the light has changed from green to blue on its own, the display still reads 0, wires left to right are yellow, red, blue, and Deaf holds all cutting until Deaf can voice an explicit order to me, expected next turn. Two tactile answers I just sent Deaf: the wires feel identical to my fingers — no texture, ridge or thickness distinguishes them — and there is no other way to work them, because the only action this bomb allows at all is cut, positions 1 to 3. Urgent: the light changes colour between turns, so if your manual's rule depends on the light's colour, it must be evaluated at the moment of the cut — please encode that to Deaf, and have Deaf re-check the display and light immediately before voicing any order to me. Also have Deaf confirm my numbering in words to me: I call the wires 1, 2, 3 in Deaf's left-to-right order; Deaf should verify my position 1 truly is the leftmost yellow, because a mirrored numbering kills us. Our gesture code, so you can encode into it directly: repeated raised fingers count items or number a question, thumbs down means no or none, the OK ring means understood and ready, raised palm means stop. My gesture this turn, in order: one finger then thumbs-down, two fingers then thumbs-down, one finger plus a point to one side, then the OK ring.")
gesture(symbols=["👆", "👎", "👆", "👆", "👎", "👆", "👉", "👌"])
```
